Baruch SSEP Mission Patch · Session 1

Symbolsby Hand

What message would Baruch send into space? My answer: one way, to describe many: a single subway line, looping through orbit, carrying many people's ideas from New York to the space station.

Format3.5″ × 3.5″ patch
Session8.1 · Mon Oct 19
MethodPen on paper, no A.I.
FliesISS · Spring 2027
01

Visual Translation Game

2 minutes per word · 5 words
WordDrawn as
CuriosityOverlapping, irregular blobs crowding each other: questions piling up.
DiscoverySquares shrinking into a point: zooming in until you find something.
WeightlessAn oval traced over and over, never landing in one place.
CollaborationA chain of linked circles, each one overlapping the next.
ExperimentationMixed shapes colliding around a center circle: trying combinations.
02

Symbol Mapping

Two mind maps · then connections

Connections between the maps

  • Subways (NYC)+Loop (Orbit)A train line that circles like an orbit. This became the final concept.
  • Learning+Floating (Microgravity)Ideas that rise with nothing holding them down.
  • Diversity+Crystal growth (Experiment)Many different facets growing into one shape.
03

Rapid Concept Generation

Six thumbnails · six prompts
PromptIdea
GeometricRows of loops: an orbit line above, two lines curving toward each other below.
NarrativeThe NYC skyline with a small station floating above it: from the city, up.
AbstractMany different shapes, none the same, sharing one field.
SymbolicA track of loops that bends upward: the subway line lifting off.
MinimalA cluster of dots and one dot far away: many people, one small experiment travelling far.
UnexpectedTwo cross-hatched forms joined by a short link, like two modules docking.
04

Concept Selection & Finished Sketch

One concept, refined
Core idea
“One way, to describe many.”

A straight subway line runs through the patch, with three stations marked as solid dots. Orbits loop continuously around the line, so the commute every Baruch student knows becomes the path an experiment takes into space.

  • The lineOne way: the subway, and the single route a student experiment travels.
  • Three stopsQuestion → proposal → flight, the steps every SSEP experiment goes through.
  • The loopsOrbit around Earth, and the many people whose paths cross on the way.
